([[Tilton, New Hampshire]]) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2012–2013) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = 2013 | career_end = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = *[[Southeastern Conference|All-SEC First Team]] ([[2012–13 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|2013]]) *[[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Rookie of the Year]] ([[2012–13 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|2013]]) *[[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2012 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2012]]) | stat1label = | stat1value = | stat2label = | stat2value = | stat3label = | stat3value = | letter = | bbr = }} '''Nerlens Noel''' (born April 10, 1994) is an [[United States|American]] former [[college basketball]] player. Noel, a son of [[Haiti]]an immigrants to the U.S.,Thamel, Pete (March 10, 2012) [http://www.nytimes.com/2012/03/11/sports/ncaabasketball/everybody-wants-a-piece-of-nerlens-noel.html Everybody Wants a Piece of Nerlens Noel]. ''New York Times'' played one season at the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|University of Kentucky]]. He plays [[Center (basketball)|center]], and was one of the top high school basketball players in the class of 2012. He is known for his trademark [[hi-top fade]] hairstyle.{{cite web|url=http://www.usabasketball.com/mens/hoopsummit/12_hsum_feature_noel.html|title=Nike Hoop Summit Player Profile: Nerlens Noel|accessdate=March 22, 2012|date=March 19, 2012|work=usabasketball.com}} ==Early Life== Nerlens Noel was born in [[Everett, Massachusetts]]. He attended [[Everett High School (Massachusetts)|Everett High School]] for two years before transferring to [[Tilton School]] in [[Tilton, New Hampshire]]. Nerlens has two older brothers. Jim, a [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] for the [[Seattle Seahawks]] of the [[National Football League]] and Rodman, a [[linebacker]] for [[NC State Wolfpack football|North Carolina State]].[http://articles.centralkynews.com/2012-09-27/amnews/34132688_1_nerlens-noel-uk-basketball-hard-work "UK Basketball: College sports is a family affair for Nerlens Noel and two older brothers"] ==High school career== Noel spent his first two years of high school at Everett High School. After his sophomore year, he transferred to Tilton. Noel was originally a part of the class of 2013, but reclassified to the 2012 college recruiting class.{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2012/02/nerlens-noel-is-now-a-senior-reclassifies-to-2012-class/|title=Nerlens Noel is Now a Senior, Reclassifies to 2012 Class|accessdate=March 22, 2012|date=February 2, 2012|publisher=SLAM Online|author=}} He was rated as the #1 player in the class of 2012 by ESPN{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/playerrankings/_/class/2012/order/true|title=ESPNU 100 – Class of 2012|accessdate=March 22, 2012|date=|publisher=ESPN|author=}} and Scout.com,{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2012|title=Scout.com Basketball Rankings – 2012|accessdate=March 22, 2012|date=|publisher=Scout.com|author=}} and the #2 player by SLAM.{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2012/01/slam-fresh-50-2012-4/|title=SLAM Fresh 50 – 2012|accessdate=March 22, 2012|date=|publisher=SLAM Online|author=}} Noel was selected to play in the 2012 [[Nike Hoop Summit]]{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/news-rumors/other-news/2012/03/us-rosters-announced-for-2012-nike-hoop-summit/|title=US Rosters Announced for 2012 Nike Hoop Summit|accessdate=March 22, 2012|date=March 9, 2012|publisher=SLAM Online|author=}} and the 2012 [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/high-school/boys-basketball/post/_/id/2936/noel-added-to-jordan-classic-roster|title=Noel added to Jordan Classic roster|accessdate=March 22, 2012|date=March 14, 2012|publisher=''[[ESPN.com]]''|author=Jordan, Jason}} Noel played high school basketball at the [[Tilton School]] in [[Tilton, New Hampshire]].[http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/7T4_J5xWREOBs3wklmWk-Q/basketball-winter-11-12/profile-nerlens-noel.htm Nerlens Noel's Tilton School 11–12 Basketball Profile]. MaxPreps.com. Retrieved on March 27, 2013. ==College career== Noel decided in April 2012 that he would be going to the [[University of Kentucky]] to play [[NCAA]] [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] basketball. He made his verbal commitment by revealing the UK logo shaved in the back of his head on national television.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/recruiting/story/_/id/7803636/no-1-recruit-nerlens-noel-chooses-play-kentucky-wildcats|title=Nerlens Noel chooses Kentucky|accessdate=April 12, 2012|date=April 11, 2012|publisher=ESPN|author=Paul Biancardi}} Since Noel was well known for his elite shot blocking abilities, fans and the media had high expectations for him to fill the shoes of [[Anthony Davis (basketball)|Anthony Davis]], who had just led the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky Wildcats]] to a national championship in the previous season, was the 2011–2012 National Player of the Year in the NCAA, set a Kentucky and NCAA freshman single-season block record with 186. In his third game on Nov 16, 2012, he accumulated 15 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 block, and 4 steals against [[2012–13 Lafayette Leopards men's basketball team|Lafayette]]. On Jan 12, 2013, although Kentucky lost the game against [[2012–13 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]], Noel recorded 15 points, 11 rebounds, 7 blocks, 6 assists, and 4 steals. On January 29, 2013, Noel set the UK single-game record with 12 blocks in a 87–74 team victory over #16 [[2012–13 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]]. 5 of the blocks happened while Noel had 4 personal fouls, and two of them were slam dunk attempts. The UK school record was previously 9 blocks in one game, set by [[Sam Bowie]] in 1981 and was then tied by [[Andre Riddick]] in 1993. Although he recorded only two points, Ole Miss coach Andy Kennedy said in the post-game press conference that "[Noel] was the difference in the game" and that he is "an incredible defensive presence." Ole Miss senior forward Murphy Holloway added that he believes Nerlens Noel is the "best shot blocker [he has] played against," including Anthony Davis. On February 12, 2013, in a game against the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]], Noel tore the [[Anterior crucial ligament|ACL]] in his left knee after blocking a Florida lay-up, forcing him to sit out the remainder of the season. Before his injury, it was projected that he would be the 1st overall pick in the [[2013 NBA Draft]]. Despite his injury, Noel decided to declare for the 2013 draft on April 15, 2013. It is also said by scouts that his draft stock will not be badly affected, if at all, by declaring for this year. Nerlens Noel has also been honored with many awards this year including, SEC Freshman Of The Year, SEC Defensive Player Of The Year, SEC First Team, SEC All Fresman Team, SEC Community Service Team. In addition to earning All-SEC first team honors by the league’s coaches, Noel earned first-team honors from the Associated Press. The AP has honored at least one UK freshman on the first team in four-consecutive seasons. Cousins and Wall both claimed the honor in 2010. [[Terrence Jones]], was an honorable mention AP selection in 2011, and both Davis and Kidd-Gilchrist were honored a season ago. Noel was also named a Freshman All-American by Sporting News, and USBWA. The Wildcats’ 6-foot-11 center was joined by [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels men's basketball|UNLV Runnin' Rebels]]’s [[Anthony Bennett (basketball)|Anthony Bennett]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]’s [[Shabazz Muhammad]], [[Oklahoma State Cowboys men's basketball|Oklahoma State Cowboys]]’s [[Marcus Smart]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]'s [[Ben McLemore]] on the Freshman All-America team. He was the fifth UK player under coach [[John Calipari]] to earn the honor from the USBWA, including [[John Wall (basketball)|John Wall]], [[DeMarcus Cousins]], [[Anthony Davis (basketball)|Anthony Davis]], and [[Michael Kidd-Gilchrist]].{{cite web|url=http://www.wildcatworld.com/2013/03/26/nerlens-noel-hauls-in-additional-postseason-accolades/|title=Nerlens Noel hauls in additional postseason accolades|work=wildcatworld.com|date=March 26, 2013|accessdate=May 17, 2013}} ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2012–13 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2012–13]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] | 24 || 24 || 31.9 || .590 || .000 || .529 || 9.5 || 1.6 || 2.1 || 4.4 || 10.5 |- | style="text-align:left;"| Career | style="text-align:left;"| | 24 || 24 || 31.9 || .590 || .000 || .529 || 9.5 || 1.6 || 2.1 || 4.4 || 10.5 {{S-end}} ==Professional Career== ===2013 NBA Draft=== He entered the draft after playing one season at the University of Kentucky and is projected to be one of the top draft picks of the [[2013 NBA Draft]].
